name: Columellar strut graft

lead: A columellar strut is a small cartilage graft placed between the medial crura in the columella during rhinoplasty to support the nasal tip. It is hidden under the skin and invisible after healing.

The chain: a concealed cartilage post gives a firmer, supported tip, which helps hold tip shape and position. Surgeons have long assumed it increases tip projection, and a retrospective review of 100 consecutive primary rhinoplasties examined its effect on projection and rotation. Surgeons also compare it with the caudal septal extension graft, which some describe as offering more control of tip position.

paras: It is done as part of a rhinoplasty, using the patient's own cartilage. Many surgeons now also use septal extension grafts. The tip's final shape settles as swelling resolves over months.

Risks are those of rhinoplasty in general, and revision surgery accounts for roughly 5 to 20 percent of operations. Graft-specific rates were not reported in the sources reviewed. It is a surgical procedure.

angle.text: Rhinoplasty patients get this concealed cartilage post to hold the nasal tip firm and in a defined position. The change is visible after healing, though surgeons debate how much it raises the tip compared with septal extension grafts.

lead: A columellar strut graft is a piece of cartilage placed between the medial crura of the lower lateral cartilages in the columella, the strip of tissue between the nostrils, during rhinoplasty to support the nasal tip. Surgeons describe it as a popular form of invisible graft because it is hidden beneath the skin [1].

It has traditionally been assumed to increase tip projection, but a retrospective review of 100 consecutive primary rhinoplasties examined its actual effect on tip projection and rotation [2]. Surgeons have also compared the strut with the caudal septal extension graft, which some describe as offering more control of tip position [3][4][5].
The evidence is mainly surgeon case series and comparative retrospective studies, along with some small registered trials.
infobox: Primary and revision rhinoplasty, usually open approach

paras: The graft is typically a small cartilage strip, commonly harvested from the septum, set between the medial crura like a post under the tip. Surgeons use it with suture techniques to shape the nasal tip [1][6]. General rhinoplasty references list the columellar strut and septal extension graft as the two main ways of supporting the tip, noting that the septal extension graft is described as offering more control and less change over time [7].

A 100-case retrospective analysis of one surgeon's primary rhinoplasties focused on whether the strut changes tip projection and rotation, challenging the historical assumption that it raises projection [2]. A comparative quantitative study measured tip position changes with the strut versus a caudal septal extension graft [3], and another study compared the effects of the two on tip support [4]. An older study sought to quantify surgical changes in tip support [8]. A review of the changing role of septal extension versus columellar grafts describes how tip projection depends on several anatomical factors, including lower lateral cartilage strength, the suspensory ligament and attachments to the upper lateral cartilage [5].

Registered trials include a planned comparison of septal extension graft versus columellar strut (NCT06958575, 60 participants, not yet recruiting) [9], a study of lateral crural steal with a columellar strut (NCT07317947, 22 participants, recruiting) [10], and a completed comparison of a septal advancement flap with a strut (NCT06370455, 30 participants) [11]. No results were found for these. Published human data are largely retrospective surgeon series [2][3][4].

Risks are those of rhinoplasty generally. Reviews report revision rates of about 5 to 20 percent for rhinoplasty overall, with problems such as asymmetry or a hanging columella among reasons for revision [7]. Graft-specific complication rates were not reported in the sources reviewed.

timeline.event: Studies examine indications and effect on tip position in primary rhinoplasty [1][2].
